thread:
anya: Heads-up: seeing a perf regression after the autotune change for MQA on H100 with paged KV layout. p99 tail latency up ~18% on our convo workload. Repro steps and a short profile below. Can someone take a look? :eyes:

samir: Oof. Is this new since the last kernel-picker rollout? Any specific model/seqlen?

anya: Yup rolled the new scoring weights yesterday. Affected model: redwood-small-v2 (MQA). Repro cmd (local perf harness):
```
./bench --model redwood-small-v2 --mode infer --batch 8 --seq-lens 64,128,512 --kv-layout paged --block-size 128 --devices h100-1
```
Baseline (old picker): p99 = 128ms, mean = 42ms. After autotune: p99 = 151ms, mean = 48ms.

liam: Can you paste the profiler flame or kernel timeline? Even a tiny snippet helps.

anya: Short profiler excerpt (timeline counts in microseconds):
```
attn_kern_K1 (gqa-path):  avg=320us  p95=490us
attn_kern_K2 (mqa-path):  avg=410us  p95=680us  <-- chosen more often now
kv_copy_read:            avg=45us
kv_page_miss_work:       avg=120us (spikes when block misaligned)
other:                   avg=80us
```
Note K2 being picked for medium seqlens (256-512) even when kv page layout is interleaved.

maggie: That's likely the KV layout interaction. We changed the paged interleaving default in the runtime last sprint (to reduce fragmentation). The kernel scorer doesn't include `kv.page_block_size` or `kv.layout_type` in the key. So autotune thinks K2 generalizes better but misses the higher copy/miss cost.

samir: Makes sense. Quick mitigation: force kernel override for MQA on H100 for seqlen >= 256 until we fix the scorer. Add a temp config: `kernel_picker.force_map["redwood-small-v2"]=K1` or set `seqlen_threshold=999`?

liam: I can run a canary with forced mapping. Also want to test bumping the page block size to 256 to see if copy/miss cost drops. Two experiments: (A) force K1, (B) block_size=256 + default picker.

perfbot: nightly-regression-bot: detected delta -> p99 +18% on redwood-small-v2 (MQA). Autotune pick changed: K1->K2 for seqlen range 256..512. Confidence=0.86. Related PR: #4122 rolled picker weights.

anya: Thanks. Action items: (1) @liam run canary A/B and paste bench outputs here, (2) @maggie can you add `kv.page_block_size` and `kv.layout_type` to the autotune feature vector so the scorer sees layout, (3) @samir add hotfix override to canary config to roll back pick for affected model.

maggie: On it. Quick note: adding KV features to the scoring vector is low-risk but will need reindexing of cached scores. I think we can keep cached entries but include a fallback mismatch penalty (-inf -> force re-eval).

samir: I'll draft the override PR and can attach a smoke test. Draft command to run smoke:
```
./smoke_test --model redwood-small-v2 --picker-override K1 --runs 100 --seq-len 512 --devices h100-1
```

liam: Canary results (A — force K1): p99=126ms mean=44ms. (B — block_size=256): p99=134ms mean=45ms. Default (no change): p99=151ms. So forcing K1 restores baseline. Block_size helps but doesn't fully recover.

anya: Great data, thanks. That supports the hypothesis that picker mis-ranked kernels for the paged-interleaved layout.

maggie: I'll instrument the scorer to include `kv.layout_type` and `kv.page_block_size` flags and push a small PR. We should also add a unit test that verifies the picker picks different kernels for `paged:interleaved` vs `paged:stripe` when the profiler indicates high kv_copy cost.

samir: I'll open the override PR and queue it for canary today. If canary is green, we'll roll to prod and merge the layout-aware scorer later this week.

anya: Perfect. Leaving this thread open for results. TY all :rocket:
